text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- Prime minister Mart Siimann admitted that half of the former KGB files left in Estonia are missing. Out of 87,000 files, only 48,846 have remained.
- The parliament rejected the Reform Party's bid to exclude the custom tariffs draft law from the agenda.
- President Lennart Meri described the NATO-Russian agreement as major event which will end the cool relations between Russia and the democratic world.
- The government intends to establish the status of state language teacher to provide better incentives for Estonian language teachers in northeastern Estonia.
- Tallinn Boys Choir has returned from Japan after a week-long tour. The concerts were described as a great success.
- Baltic defence forces commanders are meeting in Riga on May 19-20 in order to discuss cooperation.
- A British surgeon made an unusual hip-bone operation in Tartu recently, enabling a young woman to walk after she had been crippled in a car crash.
- A large collection of old coins was stolen from the Paide museum last Wednesday. The value of the collection is estimated at one million kroons.
- An Estonian business delegation left for Ukraine on Monday. They will attend an international food fair and an economic seminar.
